newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Chernogorneft may increase charter capital.
newsitem.headline: Russian Chernogorneft may increase charter capital.

text.p: Russian oil company Chernogorneft could raise its charter capital 100 times to 267.7 billion roubles from 2.7 billion, a spokesman for parent company SIDANKO said on Thursday.

"Shareholders voted changes in authorised capital in the company charter (at the annual meeting earlier this month), allowing the future possibility of a 100-fold increase charter capital," company press secretary Olga Sergeyeva said.
She did not say when new shares might be issued.
"Concrete decisions linked to carrying out a share issue will be dictated by the financial position and tasks which the (SIDANKO) holding company puts in front of Chernogorneft," Sergeyeva said.

NK SIDANKO owns 50.73 percent of Chernogorneft shares, Renaissance Nominees (Cyprus) owns 21.27 percent, the Bank of New York Nominees owns 12.83 percent, the International Bank of Bermuda Limited owns 1.68 percent, Bank MFK (ICFI) owns 1.77 percent and other legal entities own 6.72 percent.
Company employees own 3.28 percent of shares and other individuals own 1.72 percent.
